**Reviewer:** boundary-reviewer

```
The spec states a corrupt leftover .beads/ (not a valid registered worktree per git worktree list --porcelain) is deleted first, then git worktree add runs - but never states the deletion mechanism. lib/worktree.mjs::remove() (the repos only existing worktree-teardown code) uses git worktree remove [--force], specifically because a plain filesystem delete of a worktree directory leaves stale admin state in .git/worktrees/<name>, which then makes a later git worktree add at that path fail (git refuses to re-register a path with existing worktree metadata) - this is exactly the corrupt-leftover scenario this spec is trying to make resumable. The spec own corrupt-leftover premise (porcelain says NOT registered) means git worktree remove itself would likely error too, and neither the spec nor its Task Map mentions git worktree prune anywhere. Recommendation: specify the exact recovery sequence - raw filesystem removal of the .beads/ directory contents, followed by git worktree prune to clear any stale .git/worktrees/.beads registration, before git worktree add .beads beads-board is retried. Add a test fixture that simulates the interrupted-removal state and proves the retry path actually succeeds.
```
